introduction.p: When the state has several components, their rates form a system of differential equations. A spring can be described by position and velocity; interacting populations require one variable for each population. The equations couple those components through their rates of change.

exercise.title: Why do two interacting populations require a system?

statement.p: A single equation P'=rP uses one number as the state. Rabbits and wolves need two. In your own words, why are the equations coupled, and why can you not solve one population first and then the other?

hint.p: Each derivative depends on both unknowns. The two populations move together, so a solution is a pair of functions on the same time interval.

subsection.p: When wolves are few, rabbits increase. Then the abundance of rabbits lets wolves increase. More wolves reduce the rabbits. With fewer rabbits, wolves decline. Then the rabbits can recover.
The equations do not describe one population rising or falling by itself. They describe a moving point in the plane.

paragraphs.title: A numerical glimpse
paragraphs.p: Both populations are increasing, but rabbits are increasing faster. In the phase plane, the point initially moves mostly to the right and slightly upward.
Both populations are decreasing. The point moves left and down.
This is the system version of a direction field. Instead of little line segments with a slope, we draw little arrows with two components.

note.title: Phase plane
note.p: the phase plane is the (x,y)-plane together with direction arrows
A solution traces a curve in this plane as time passes.

paragraphs.p: The phase plane does not usually give exact formulas for R(t) and W(t). It gives the shape of the interaction.
That is often the first thing we need.

exercise.title: What does a phase plane show that a pair of time graphs does not?

statement.p: For a system, the state is a point (x,y), and the right-hand side supplies an arrow at each point. In your own words, why is a solution a moving point in that plane, and what information is missing from the phase-plane picture?

hint.p: Time is the parameter that traces the curve; it need not appear as an axis. The picture shows the shape of the interaction more than exact formulas for x(t) and y(t).

note.title: The bridge
note.p: A solution of a system is a moving point:
So differential equations lead naturally to parametrized curves, vector fields, and functions of several variables.

subsection.p: This is where single-variable calculus begins to lean toward the next subject. The derivative of one function was enough for motion on a line. Motion in a plane needs two coordinate functions. Interactions need functions of several variables. The geometry of change begins to expand.

Before leaving differential equations, we should collect the warnings that protect the methods we have used: solutions can be lost by division, numerical methods can invent false behavior, and the same differential equation can describe many different histories until an initial condition chooses one.

exercise.title: Why do systems lead naturally to multivariable calculus?

statement.p: Even the oscillator y''+\omega^2 y=0 can be rewritten as a first-order system for (y,v). In your own words, why does that change the meaning of state from one number to a point, and what new kind of function then appears on the right-hand side?

hint.p: The right-hand side is built from functions of several variables. Parametrized curves and vector fields are the geometry of that moving point.
